chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who was found killed, then two men came to his heir. One of them said, “I killed him intentionally,” and the other said, “I killed him by mistake.” He said: “If he accepts the statement of the one who claims intentional killing, then he has no recourse against the one who claims mistaken killing. And if he accepts the statement of the one who claims mistaken killing, then he has no recourse against the one who claims intentional killing.”

key_terms.سَبِيلٌ: a legal avenue, claim, or recourse against someone
key_terms.عَمْدًا: intentionally, with deliberate intent to kill
key_terms.وَلِيِّهِ: the slain person's heir or legal representative

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when two men separately confess to one killing, one claiming intentional homicide and the other mistaken homicide?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling concerning a homicide case in which two different men each confess to the killing, one as intentional and the other as accidental. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام rules that the heir must proceed according to one of the two claims, and once one is taken, no claim remains against the other.
